text:
The rate constant (k) of a reaction is measured at different temperatures (T), and the data are
plotted in the given figure. The activation energy of the reaction in kJ mol$^{–1}$ is : 

(R is gas constant)

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the Arrhenius equation, $\ln k=\ln A-\dfrac{E_{a}}{RT}$, which can be written as

$\ln k=\ln A-\dfrac{E_{a}}{10^{3}R}\left (\dfrac{10^{3}}{T}\right )$

So the plot of $\ln k$ against $\dfrac{10^{3}}{T}$ is a straight line of slope $-\dfrac{E_{a}}{10^{3}R}$.

From the graph, $\ln k$ falls from 10 at $\dfrac{10^{3}}{T}=0$ to 0 at $\dfrac{10^{3}}{T}=5$, so the slope is $-\dfrac{10}{5}=-2$.

$\dfrac{E_{a}}{10^{3}R}=2\Rightarrow E_{a}=2000R\text{J mol}^{-1}=2R\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
Consider the complex ions,

trans-[$Co(en)_{2}Cl_{2}$]$^{+} (A)$ and
 cis-[$Co(en)_{2}Cl_{2}$]$^{+} (B)$.

The correct statement regarding them is :
options: both (A) and (B) can be optically active.
both (A) and (B) can not be optically active.

(A) can not be optically active, but (B) can
be optically active.

(A) can be optically active, but (B) can not
be optically active.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
trans-[$Co(en)_{2}Cl_{2}$]$^{+}$ contain a plane of
symmetry. It cannot be optically active.

cis-[$Co(en)_{2}Cl_{2}$]$^{+}$ does not contain
any plane of symmetry. Hence the compound (B) is
optically active.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
The correct order of the ionic radii of
 $O^{2–}, N^{3–}, F^{–}$
, $Mg^{2+}, Na^{+}$ and $Al^{3+}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For isoelectronic species, as the no. of protons
increases, size of ions decreases.

$\therefore$ Correct order of size for isoelectronic species

$Al^{3+} < Mg^{2+} < Na^{+} < F^{–}$
 $< O^{2–} < N^{3–}$

text:
The increasing order of boiling points of the following compounds is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(I) Shows hydrogen bonding from –OH group only.

(II)  Shows strongest hydrogen bonding from both sides of –OH group as well as $–NO_{2}$ group.

(III) Shows stronger hydrogen bonding from both side of –OH group as well as $–NH_{2}$ group.

(IV)  Shows stronger hydrogen bonding from one side –OH group and another side of –OCH$_{3}$ group shows only
dipole-dipole interaction.

Hence correct order of boiling point is :

I < IV < III < II

text:
The volume, in mL, of $0.02 M K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7}$ solution
required to react with 0.288 g of ferrous
oxalate in acidic medium is $_______$.

(Molar mass of Fe = 56 g mol$^{–1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7} +$ FeC$_{2}O_{4}$ $\to$ $Cr^{+3} + Fe^{+3} + CO_{2}$

$n_{$factor} of $K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7} = 3$ $\times$ 2 = 6

$n_{$factor} of FeC$_{2}O_{4} = 1 + 2 = 3$

m. eq. of $K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7} = m. eq$. of FeC$_{2}O_{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{6\times 0.02\times vol}{1000}$ = $\frac{0.288}{144}\times 3$

$\Rightarrow$ vol = 50 ml
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot

text:
Considering that $\Delta_{0}$
 > P, the magnetic moment
 (in BM) of [$Ru(H_{2}O)_{6}$]$^{2+}$ would be $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ru(44) : [Kr] $4d^{7}5s^{1}$

$Ru^{+2} =$ [Kr]$4d^{6}$

As $\Delta_{0}$
 > P,

$\therefore$ Pairing of $e^{–}s$ will take place.

No. of unpaired $e^{–}s = 0$

$\therefore$ Magnetic moment = 0 B.M

text:
The number of chiral carbons present in
sucrose is $_____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Sucrose is α-D-glucopyranose joined through its C-1 to C-2 of β-D-fructofuranose.

Glucose unit: C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4 and C-5 each carry four different groups, so it has 5 chiral carbons; C-6 ($\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$) is not chiral.

Fructose unit: C-2 (bonded to the glycosidic O, the ring O, C-1 and C-3), C-3, C-4 and C-5 are chiral, so it has 4 chiral carbons; C-1 and C-6 are $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ groups and are not chiral.

Total number of chiral carbons $=5+4=9$.

Hence, the answer is 9.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 5th September Evening Slot
